'''Uma Chowdhry''' (1947 – January 7, 2024) was an American [[chemist]] whose career was spent in research and management positions with [[DuPont|E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company]].<ref name="OH"/><ref name="transcript"/> She specialized in the science of [[ceramic materials]], including [[catalysts]],<ref>Machiels, C. J.; Chowdhry, U.; Staley, R. H.; Ohuchi, F.; Sleight, A. W.   Formaldehyde from methanol.  Catal. Convers. Synth. Gas Alcohols Chem., [Proc. Symp.] (1984), 413-18.</ref><ref>Contractor, R. M.; Bergna, H. E.; Horowitz, H. S.; Blackstone, C. M.; Malone, B.; Torardi, C. C.; Griffiths, B.; Chowdhry, U.; Sleight, A. W.  Butane oxidation to maleic anhydride over vanadium phosphate catalysts.  Catalysis Today (1987), 1(1-2), 49-58.</ref> [[proton conductor]]s,<ref>Chowdhry, U.; Barkley, J. R.; English, A. D.; Sleight, A. W. New inorganic proton conductors.  Materials Research Bulletin  (1982),  17(7),  917-33.</ref> [[superconductors]]<ref>Sleight, Arthur W.; Chowdhry, Uma. Superconductivity and the metal-semiconductor transition.  Advanced Ceramic Materials  (1987),  2(3B),  713-18.</ref><ref>Subramanian, M. A.; Torardi, C. C.; Calabrese, J. C.; Gopalakrishnan, J.; Morrissey, K. J.; Askew, T. R.; Flippen, R. B.; Chowdhry, U.; Sleight, A. W.  A new high-temperature superconductor:  Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>3−x</sub>Ca<sub>x</sub>Cu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8</sub><sup>+y</sup>.  Science (Washington, DC, United States)  (1988),  239(4843),  1015-17.</ref><ref>Torardi, C. C.; Subramanian, M. A.; Calabrese, J. C.; Gopalakrishnan, J.; Morrissey, K. J.; Askew, T. R.; Flippen, R. B.; Chowdhry, U.; Sleight, A. W.   Crystal structure of Tl<sub>2</sub>Ba<sub>2</sub>Ca<sub>2</sub>Cu<sub>3</sub>O<sub>10</sub>, a 125 K superconductor.  Science (Washington, DC, United States)  (1988),  240(4852),  631-4.</ref> and ceramic packaging for [[microelectronics]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1146/annurev.ms.17.080187.001543|title=Ceramic Substrates for Microelectronic Packaging|year=1987|last1=Chowdhry|first1=U.|last2=Sleight|first2=A. W.|journal=[[Annual Review of Materials Science]]|volume=17|pages=323–340|bibcode=1987AnRMS..17..323C}}</ref><ref>Subramanian, M. A.; Corbin, D. R.; Chowdhry, U..   Zeolites as precursors to aluminosilicate-based ceramics for microelectronic packaging.    Advances in Ceramics  (1989),  26(Ceram. Substrates Packages Electron. Appl.),  239-47.</ref>

==Early life and education==
Chowdhry was born in [[Mumbai]], [[India]], in 1947. She received a [[bachelor's degree]] in physics from the University of Bombay (now [[Mumbai University]]) in 1968 before coming to the United States.   She received a [[Master of Science|Master of Science degree]] from the [[California Institute of Technology]] (Caltech) in engineering science in 1970.  After two years with [[Ford Motor Company]], she entered the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) where she earned a [[Ph.D.]] in materials science in 1976.<ref name="Profile">{{cite web|title=Uma Chowdhry|url=https://www.sciencehistory.org/historical-profile/uma-chowdhry|website=Science History Institute |date=29 June 2016|access-date=21 March 2018}}</ref><ref name="OH">{{cite web |author=Center for Oral History |title=Uma Chowdhry |url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/nt2ydj8 |website=[[Science History Institute]]}}</ref><ref name="transcript">{{cite book |last=Domush |first=Hilary |url=https://digital.sciencehistory.org/works/nt2ydj8 |title=Uma Chowdhry, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by Hilary Domush at Experimental Station Wilmington, Delaware on 24 and 25 August 2011 |date=25 August 2011 |publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] |place=Philadelphia, PA}}</ref>

==Career==
===DuPont===
She joined DuPont in 1977 as a research scientist<ref name="IRI">{{cite news|title=DuPont's Uma Chowdhry honored with Industrial Research Institute's 2011 Medal|url=http://www.iriweb.org/articles/dupont%E2%80%99s-uma-chowdhry-honored-industrial-research-institute%E2%80%99s-2011-medal|access-date=21 March 2018|work=Innovation Research Interchange|date=26 May 2011|archive-date=22 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322081539/http://www.iriweb.org/articles/dupont%E2%80%99s-uma-chowdhry-honored-industrial-research-institute%E2%80%99s-2011-medal|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
in [[Central Research]] & Development Department of [[DuPont|E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company]] at the [[DuPont Experimental Station]] in [[Wilmington, Delaware]]. By 1985 she had been promoted to research manager of Central Research. In 1987 she led DuPont's research effort in ceramic superconducting materials and developed a program that generated over 20 patents and 50 publications.<ref>{{cite web|title=2006 Uma Chowdhry|url=http://www2.dupont.com/Phoenix_Heritage/en_US/2006_detail.html|website=DuPont|access-date=21 March 2018|archive-date=15 February 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150215073649/http://www2.dupont.com/Phoenix_Heritage/en_US/2006_detail.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>  In 1988 she became laboratory director of the Electronics group,<ref name="OH"/><ref name="transcript"/> and by 1991 was promoted to be its director.<ref name="Hawkins"/>

The following year she was appointed laboratory director of the Jackson Laboratory for the Specialty Chemicals group.<ref name="Hawkins"/> In 1993 she became R&D director, Specialty Chemicals.<ref name="oh"/><ref name="transcript"/> in 1995 she became business director for [[terathane]] products, and two years later was promoted to Business Planning and Technology Director for Chemicals.<ref name="Hawkins"/> In 1999 she was promoted to director of DuPont Engineering Technology.<ref name="OH"/><ref name="transcript"/>

In 2006 she became senior vice president and global chief science and technology officer of DuPont,<ref name="OH"/><ref name="transcript"/><ref name="Hawkins"/> responsible for the company's core research programs and the DuPont "APEX" portfolio of research programs, including basic chemistry, materials science and biotechnology.<ref name="Hawkins">{{cite book|last1=Hawkins|first1=Carol Hooks|title=American women leaders: 1,560 current biographies|date=2009|publisher=McFarland & Co.|location=Jefferson, N.C.|isbn=978-0-7864-3847-1|page=73|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VpYZDgAAQBAJ&pg=PA73}}</ref> She retired in September 2010, becoming chief science and technology officer emeritus.<ref name="NIST">{{cite journal|title=DuPont Scientist Joins NIST Advisory Group|url=https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2010/09/dupont-scientist-joins-nist-advisory-group|journal=NIST|date=28 September 2010}}</ref>

In response to contamination of Ohio river caused by [[perfluorooctanoic acid]] (PFOA, also known as C8), the key ingredient in Teflon, and subsequent cases of cancer and other medical issues, when asked if this C8 chemical could be responsible for babies born with deformities in 2 out of 8 former DuPont women employees, Ms. Uma responded "In the realm of scientific facts, this is not considered a statistically significant sample."<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20220413150749/https://thedevilweknow.com/ Article title]}}  {{nonspecific|date=June 2022}}</ref>

===Other contributions===
Chowdhry served on study groups for the [[National Research Council (United States)|National Research Council]] to assess various technology topics of national interest, and was a member of National Research Council's Committee on Globalization (2004). Chowdhry was a member of the National Committee on Women in Science and Engineering sponsored by both the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Engineering]] since 1999.<ref name="Facilitating">{{cite book |title=Facilitating interdisciplinary research|date=2005|publisher=National Academies Press|location=Washington|isbn=978-0-309-09435-1|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ObxTAgAAQBAJ&pg=PA233|access-date=21 March 2018}}</ref><ref name="XXcellence">{{cite book|author=National Research Council|title=Achieving XXcellence in Science: Role of Professional Societies in Advancing Women in Science: Proceedings of a Workshop|chapter=Committee on Women in Science and Engineering, Policy and Global Affairs Division, National Research Council |date=2004|publisher=The National Academies Press|location=Washington, DC|url=https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK25364/}}</ref><ref name="Beyond">{{cite book |title=Beyond bias and barriers: fulfilling the potential of women in academic science and engineering|date=2007|publisher=National Academies Press|location=Washington, D.C.|isbn=978-0-309-10042-7|edition=[Online-Ausg.]|doi=10.17226/11741 |pmid=20669424 |url=https://www.nap.edu/read/11741/chapter/1}}</ref><ref name="Rising">{{cite book |doi=10.17226/11463 |doi-access=free |page=vi |title=Rising Above the Gathering Storm |year=2007 |publisher=National Academies Press|location=Washington, D.C. |isbn=978-0-309-18758-9 }}</ref>

She served on the board of directors for the [[Industrial Research Institute]] (2002-2005),<ref name="IRI"/> Baxter International Inc. (2012-),<ref name="Baxter">{{cite news|title=Baxter Appoints Two New Directors to Its Board|url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20120927006447/en|work=BusinessWire|date=27 September 2012}}</ref> 
LORD Corporation (2010-),<ref name="LORD">{{cite news|title=LORD Corporation Names Chowdhry to Board of Directors|url=https://www.coatingsworld.com/issues/2010-09/view_people-in-the-news/lord-corporation-names-chowdhry-to-board-of-direct|access-date=21 March 2018|work=Coatings World|date=15 September 2010|archive-date=22 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180322020307/https://www.coatingsworld.com/issues/2010-09/view_people-in-the-news/lord-corporation-names-chowdhry-to-board-of-direct|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
the Advisory Board for Advanced Technology at the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology|National Institute of Standards]] (NIST, 2010),<ref name="NIST"/><ref name="IRI"/>
the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]]<ref name="Facilitating"/> and the Laboratory Operations Board for the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] for the US Government.<ref name="Facilitating"/> She was appointed to the Laboratory Operations Board for the U.S. Department of Energy, Washington, D.C., in 2002.

Chowdhry served on advisory boards of engineering schools at MIT, [[University of Pennsylvania]], [[Princeton University]] and the [[University of Delaware]].<ref name="Facilitating"/>

Uma Chowdhry and her husband, Vinay Chowdhry, lived in Wilmington, Delaware.<ref name="Profile"/> She was elected to the board of trustees for [[Christiana Care Health System|Christiana Care Health Services]] in Delaware in 2003.

Chowdhry died on January 7, 2024, after a long illness preceded by a stroke.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Uma Chowdhry - Obituaries in Wilmington, DE {{!}} The News Journal |url=https://delawareonline.com/obituaries/pdov0694088 |access-date=2024-06-18 |website=delawareonline.com |date=19 January 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
For her contributions to the science of ceramics, Chowdhry was elected Fellow of the [[American Ceramic Society]] in 1989,<ref>{{cite web|title=Fellows of the American Ceramic Society|url=http://ceramics.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/02/fellows_recipients_20141.pdf|website=Ceramics.org|access-date=20 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Ceramic">{{cite book|last1=The American Ceramic Society|title=Successful women in ceramics and glass science and engineering|date=2016|publisher=John Wiley|location=[S.l.]|isbn=978-1-118-73360-8|pages=85–88|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JPSlCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA86|chapter=Profile 15: Uma Chowdhry}}</ref> where she chaired the academy's emerging technologies committee, 2002&ndash;2004.

She was elected a member to the National Academy of Engineering in 1996 for the application of advanced ceramic technologies to novel catalyst structures, large-scale chemical synthesis, and multilayer electronic circuit manufacture.<ref>{{cite web|title=NAE Members|url=https://www.nae.edu/30065.aspx|website=National Academy of Engineering|access-date=20 November 2016}}</ref> Besides her membership, she served on the program advisory board and election subcommittees.  She was also elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=Biography of Dr. Uma Chowdhry|url=https://www.nist.gov/office-director/biography-dr-uma-chowdhry|website=NIST|access-date=20 November 2016|archive-date=20 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120151014/https://www.nist.gov/office-director/biography-dr-uma-chowdhry|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Chowdhry received the 2011 [[IRI Medal]] for her leadership contributions at DuPont.<ref name="IRI"/><ref>[http://www.rdmag.com/News/2011/05/General-Science-DuPont-sweeps-IRIs-2011-Industry-Awards/ "DuPont Sweeps IRI's 2011 Industry Awards"], ''R&D Magazine'', 27 May 2011, accessed 8 February 2012.</ref> Chowdhry received the 2011 Earle B. Barnes Award for Leadership in Chemical Research Management from the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref>Chemical & Engineering News, 30 August 2010, page 32.</ref>
